problem: Our nightly database backup job silently skips some nights; the cron entry and the backup script have not changed in months.
instructions: Score each item with quality-rubric.md. chain lists the reasons above it, from the top; siblings are the other reasons answering the same why.

chain: A slow prior run or stale lock file makes the script exit early without dumping the database.
The lock-found branch exits with status zero and no alert, so a skipped night looks like success.
items.reason: Monitoring checks only the cron job's exit code, not the age of the newest backup file.
siblings: The skip message goes to stdout, which the crontab redirects to /dev/null with no MAILTO set.
The skip path was written for rare overlaps and never tested, so nobody reviewed how it reports itself.

chain: The cron time falls in the daylight-saving changeover hour, so that night's scheduled minute never occurs.
items.reason: The backup minute was set to 02:30 local time, inside the hour that clocks skip each spring.
siblings: Cron evaluates the schedule in the host's DST-observing local timezone instead of UTC.
The cron daemon running the job has no catch-up logic for wall-clock minutes skipped by a DST jump.

chain: The host is rebooted or suspended during the scheduled window, and cron never replays a run it missed.
Automatic OS updates are configured to reboot the host at a fixed early-morning time overlapping the backup's cron minute.
items.reason: Kernel updates require a restart because no live-patching was adopted, so auto-reboot was enabled as the default fix.
siblings: The auto-reboot time was left at the distro default and never compared against the backup entry in the crontab.
Patching and backups are owned by different people, with no shared schedule listing both jobs' times.

chain: A slow prior run or stale lock file makes the script exit early without dumping the database.
The dump and upload steps have no timeout, so a stalled run keeps holding the lock into the next night.
items.reason: The database has grown for months while the unchanged script still dumps uncompressed in one pass, lengthening every run.
siblings: The dump tool waits indefinitely for table locks held by long transactions or overnight maintenance jobs.
Uploads to the network storage mount block forever when the mount stalls, since no transfer timeout is configured.

chain: A slow prior run or stale lock file makes the script exit early without dumping the database.
items.reason: The lock file is removed only on a normal exit, so a killed or crashed run leaves it behind.
siblings: The lock-found branch exits with status zero and no alert, so a skipped night looks like success.
The dump and upload steps have no timeout, so a stalled run keeps holding the lock into the next night.

chain: The cron time falls in the daylight-saving changeover hour, so that night's scheduled minute never occurs.
The cron daemon running the job has no catch-up logic for wall-clock minutes skipped by a DST jump.
items.reason: Busybox crond documentation never mentions DST behaviour, so the gap was invisible when the image was chosen.
siblings: The backup moved into a minimal Alpine container, which ships busybox crond rather than cronie with DST compensation.
Staging runs in UTC, so no DST transition was ever exercised before the schedule reached production.

chain: The cron time falls in the daylight-saving changeover hour, so that night's scheduled minute never occurs.
Cron evaluates the schedule in the host's DST-observing local timezone instead of UTC.
items.reason: The crontab has no CRON_TZ=UTC line, so the backup entry silently inherits the system zone.
siblings: The server image sets the office's local zone so log timestamps match what on-call engineers read.
Provisioning accepted the installer's regional timezone default, and configuration management never enforces UTC on database hosts.

items.reason: The cloud provider schedules host maintenance and live-migration pauses in early-morning hours matching the backup time.
siblings: An idle power policy suspends the VM when no sessions are active, and the backup takes no sleep inhibitor lock.
A cost-saving auto-stop schedule was added to shut down low-traffic VMs overnight without checking scheduled jobs.
